This is a fun and engaging multiplayer title, especially suited for players who enjoy a competitive environment. I’ve played it on and off for several years, and during that time the skill ceiling has risen significantly, making it a strong choice for those looking to test and refine their abilities.

The game is generally kid‑friendly, though it can become toxic when teammates tilt or communication breaks down. Because of its competitive nature, I would not classify it as a casual experience. However, it remains an excellent option for coordinated play with friends.

Overall, I recommend this game to players seeking a challenging, team‑based experience rather than a laid‑back, casual one.

reviews.review: play this game and you'll have a super toxic love hate relationship with rocket league

Rocket League is easily my favourite game of all time.

I play it every day, and somehow it still never gets old. It’s one of those rare games that is incredibly simple to understand but takes years to truly master. You can always improve your mechanics, positioning, rotations, consistency and decision-making, which means there is always another reason to queue up for one more match.

What keeps me coming back is the challenge. Some days you’re playing perfectly, other days absolutely nothing goes your way, but I never give up. Every loss teaches you something, every mistake gives you something to work on, and every great match reminds you why you keep playing.

There is no better feeling than hitting a shot you’ve been practising for weeks, making a ridiculous save, pulling off the perfect pass, or winning an intense overtime match where both teams are giving everything they have.

Rocket League can definitely test your patience, especially in ranked, but that is part of what makes improving feel so rewarding. Your progress actually feels earned.

Thousands of matches later, I can still jump on and have just as much fun as I did when I started.

It’s competitive, frustrating, exciting, addictive and unbelievably satisfying.

I play every day.
I lose.
I learn.
I improve.
I queue again.

Never give up.

10/10 — See you in overtime.

Great game to compete or just to have fun getting a little better each time.  Buy stuff if you want or don't, it makes no difference if you'll win.  A single battle pass is enough to get plenty of new cars, play enough (which you likely will) and you can earn the next pass.  It's very obtainable, not one of those games that make it a job to earn. I may have over 600 hours, but that's over 6 years and I still earn the next pass.

Grab a PS5 controller, plug it in using USB to your favorite Linux gaming PC and enjoy.  When you start, just remember, everyone is terrible at first ;)
